package_info.why_malicious: The report does not describe a specific malicious software package or code artifact. Instead, it summarizes several high-profile cyberattacks, ransomware campaigns, and vulnerabilities, but does not provide code-level details or package-level indicators for extraction.

behavioral_signatures: Ransomware encrypting files and exfiltrating sensitive data (e.g., LockBit, Black Basta)
SIM swap attacks to bypass multi-factor authentication
Exploitation of zero-day vulnerabilities in network appliances (e.g., Fortinet, Ivanti)
Use of privilege escalation exploits by worms (e.g., Raspberry Robin)
Delivery of malware via malicious Office documents exploiting old vulnerabilities
file_indicators: Encrypted file extensions typical of ransomware (e.g., .lockbit, .blackbasta)
Presence of ransom notes (e.g., README.txt, LOCKBIT-README.txt)
Malicious Office documents exploiting CVE-2017-11882, CVE-2017-0199, CVE-2018-0802
network_indicators: Outbound connections to known ransomware C2 domains (LockBit, Black Basta)
Connections to webhook.site or similar exfiltration endpoints
Unusual traffic to api.github.com for token validation or repo enumeration
Traffic to traffic broker infrastructure (e.g., VexTrio)
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor for ransomware behavioral patterns such as mass file encryption, creation of ransom notes, and exfiltration of sensitive data. Detect exploitation attempts against known vulnerabilities (e.g., Fortinet, Ivanti, Linux shim) by inspecting network traffic and system logs for suspicious HTTP requests or privilege escalation attempts. Watch for SIM swap indicators and unauthorized MFA bypass. Use endpoint protection and threat emulation tools to identify known malware signatures and exploit techniques. Monitor for malicious Office documents exploiting legacy vulnerabilities and block or sandbox suspicious attachments.
